main_text.p: tus venientibus in Segor: Ita omnes illæ circū iacentes Regiones, à monte Gilead ad Mare Mediterraneum, & à Dan vsq; ad Bersabee. Permanserunt posteà longè florentiores ex ipsius Domini Geographia: Terra (inquit) ad quam ingrederis possidendum, non est sicut Terra Ægypti, de qua existi; vbi iactò semine in Hor-torum morem aquè ducuntur irrigua: Sed montosa est & campestris, de cœlo expectans pluuiam, quam Dominus Deus Tuus semper inuisit, & oculi ejus in ea sint, à principio anni vsq; ad finem eius. Sed non libet à textu peregrinari. Quod toties pollicitus est Dominus: Introducam te in terram lactē & melle fluentem, Exod.5. & passim alibi; non tantum inuenerunt Exploratores esse verissimum, Num.13. & ad oculum demonstrarunt; tot Nationes inter tam angustos limites; tot Ciuitates, quarum in sacra pagina illustris sunt Nomina; tot milites in censu Dauidico conspicui, & postea ab Abia & Ieroboam in aciem educti; sed absqz alicujus tropi pallio ostendit hic contextus. Quid saltu vepribus & dumetis horrido inculcius? Et quid Eremo desolatius? Vt Iohan-ni Baptistæ tamen in Eremo præter Locustas erat

page.notes: Marginal references in the left margin: "Deut.11." beside "Terra ... ingrederis", "Exod.3." beside "Introducam te", "2.Sam.24." beside "tot milites in censu Dauidico", "1.Chron.13." beside "Abia & Ieroboam". Note the "Deut.11." and "Exod.3." references are printed in the margin in small type; the Greek-letter mark near the bottom left is a fragment only and was not transcribed. Words "Exod.5." and "Num.13." appear inline in the text as printed. Some letters on the scan are faint (notably the final line before the catchword, and the marginal numbers), and the foot line of the page is partly obscured; text read as far as visible. The mark "[?]" was not needed for the main text as it is legible at the scale of the scan. Printed spelling kept (e.g. "pluuiam", "inuisit", "Ieroboam").
